name: Good interaction algorithm and Fourier analysis
description: An algorithm for calculating interactions in factorial experiments by successive matrix operations. Good applied analogous operations to discrete Fourier transforms, using coprime factors and Chinese-remainder indexing to reduce a one-dimensional transform to a multidimensional one.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: I. J. Good published an algorithm for factorial interactions and showed how to speed up discrete Fourier transforms, including a one-dimensional transform whose length splits into coprime factors.

evidence.supports: Dates and presents the factorial-interaction algorithm and the Fourier shortcuts, with a worked coprime index example at length 24.
Identifies the Fourier method described by Good as the prime-factor algorithm and distinguishes it from Cooley–Tukey.

events.caveats: Section 12 credits Good’s 1951 paper for the converse identification of the one-dimensional and multidimensional transforms. The 1958 paper uses the relationship to reduce the arithmetic.

evidence.supports: Good’s original summary describes an interaction algorithm and Fourier shortcuts in July 1958.

date.basis: The publisher identifies the original July 1960 issue of the journal.

events.statement: Good published an addendum clarifying inversion of the Yates algorithm and describing a discrete Poisson summation analogue for relating yields and interactions.

evidence.locator: July 1960 issue metadata and author’s Summary
evidence.supports: Dates the addendum and describes the clarification, numerical example and connection to discrete Poisson summation.

events.caveats: The author’s summary supports the publication and the stated topics. Verification of the detailed formulas requires the full article.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.

unresolved.note: Compare the original 1951 paper with 1958 §12 to determine exactly what the earlier transform identity established and whether it included a computational shortcut.
The original summary establishes the issue month and scope of the correction. Inspect the full article before attributing any new Fourier algorithm or a specific formula to it.
